_note: The WRITE ZONE of each delegation role — the machine-readable half of the prose in
.claude/agents/<role>.md. JSON takes no comments, so this is where this file is explained.
HOW IT IS MEANT TO BE USED, AND ITS READER DOES NOT EXIST YET. The intended reader is
`node tools/gates/lights/role-scope.mjs --role <role> --since <sha>` (port-plan.md:1157): it
takes the paths changed in the range and reports any that fall outside that role's 'write' list
or inside its 'neverWrite' list. That file is NOT WRITTEN as of 2026-11-01 — .claude/agents/
core.md:32, api.md, web.md and docs/knowledge/process.md all cite it in the present tense, and
today it is a command that does not run. So what this file declares is currently read by
nobody, which is said here rather than left to be discovered. It is a REPORT a human reads,
not one of the sixteen standing lights: the sixteen are in STANDING_LIGHT_IDS in
tools/gates/lib/spec-parse.mjs and this is not one of them, which is also why no light going
green or red can tell you whether this file is still true.
WHAT ITS READER MUST TAKE FOR A RANGE. Not `baseRev('main')` on its own: when HEAD is at the
base ref that merge base IS HEAD, the range is empty, and a diff-based report then finds
nothing and says so cleanly — measured in tools/gates/lights/run.mjs, which resolves the four
range kinds (since | merge-base | previous-commit | empty-tree) and is the one place that does.
ITS HONEST LIMIT. It judges the DIFF, not AUTHORSHIP. Nothing in this repository records which
session wrote a line, so 'this change was made by the role that was supposed to make it' stays
a human reading. The limit is stated here in words on purpose: the four agent files and
docs/knowledge/process.md:111 all cite 'TD-0009' for it, and TD-0009 is
docs/tech-debt/TD-0009-vendor-digests-owed.md — a different debt. There is no TD for this
limit yet, so citing a number here would be the fifth copy of a wrong reference.
A SECOND LIMIT, which is the harness's and not this file's: of everything written down here,
the ONLY part the harness itself holds is the absence of Edit and Write from the `tools:` list
of the verifier and reviewer roles. Everything else is convention — `Bash` in an allowlist
makes any command technically reachable — and .claude/settings.json is project-wide and cannot
be scoped to a role.
THE ROLE THAT IS DECLARED ABSENT. `packages/core/fixtures/**/*.json` belongs to a `fixtures`
role that is NOT WRITTEN YET (.claude/agents/core.md:30-31). It has no agent file, so it has no
entry here: an entry would read as a zone somebody owns. Until it exists, a fixture value the
spec does not state is a human's call, never a plausible invention.
ENTRY SHAPE, checked by manifestProblems() in lights/_shared.mjs:
{ "role": "<lowercase name, matching .claude/agents/<role>.md>",
"agentFile": ".claude/agents/<role>.md",
"write": ["<repo-relative path>"],      // empty is legitimate: a read-only role
"neverWrite": ["<repo-relative path>"], // narrower than 'everything else', and louder
"why": "<one sentence>" }
A path matches an entry when it equals it or lies under it. No globs — see visible.json.
'neverWrite' is not redundant with 'write': a path inside the write zone can still be forbidden
(apps/web/test/setup.ts is inside apps/web/test and is measured as mandatory as written), and a
path outside it is worth naming when getting it wrong is the expected mistake.

roles.why: Platform-free work only: rules, task model, scheduling, persistence shape, determinism. A type that needs a platform is split — the rule here, the adapter in an app — so reaching into apps/ is the mistake this zone is drawn against.
The Fastify adapter only, with no rule of its own: a branch that decides something about the product is a rule in the wrong package, so it is asked of the core role instead of written here.

The React presentation layer only, stub screens under apps/web/src/stubs/; apps/web/test/setup.ts is inside the write zone and still forbidden, because its afterEach(cleanup) is measured as mandatory and a rewrite makes a second render() in one file find the first still mounted.

Runs the checks of record and reports what the artifacts say; its only output is the run artifacts the tools themselves write under .ci/, which is gitignored and therefore never appears in a diff this report can judge.

Read-only adversarial pre-review for the human reviewer: it proposes no fix, approves nothing and changes no state, so any path in a diff attributed to it is a finding about the delegation, not about the code.
